questions.prompt: A JavaScript array `[2,10,1]` uses sort with no comparator. What result should numeric code avoid assuming?

choices.text: String-based ordering; the default comparison always uses numeric subtraction.
Any stable order; sort randomly shuffles all values before returning.
Mutation; sort always returns a fresh array without touching its receiver.
Numeric ascending order; the default comparison uses string forms.

questions.explanation: Default sort uses string comparison, producing [1,10,2] here. A numeric comparator such as (a,b)=>a-b is needed for numeric ascending order.

sources.title: ECMAScript: Indexed Collections
sources.claim: Array methods have defined mutation and comparison semantics; sorting without a comparator uses string ordering and copies can be shallow.

questions.prompt: For sorted `[1,3,3,7]`, a lower-bound search for 3 returns which insertion index?

choices.text: 3, after every element equal to the target.
4, because a present value has no valid insertion position.
1, before the first element equal to the target.
2, after the first equal element but before later duplicates.

questions.explanation: Lower bound places the target before existing equal values. Values before index 1 are below 3; values at and after it are at least 3.

sources.title: bisect: Array bisection algorithm
sources.claim: Lower-bound search partitions sorted data into values below the target and values at least the target; logarithmic search does not make array insertion logarithmic.

questions.prompt: Records have unique business IDs but may be recreated as new objects. Why might Set of the objects fail to deduplicate by ID?

choices.text: Set only deduplicates objects that have distinct reference identities.
Set compares object identity rather than the business ID field.
Set compares every object by all of its JSON fields automatically.
Set deduplicates objects by their first numeric field automatically.

questions.explanation: Set key equality does not inspect a chosen business field. Extract an explicit key when deduplication is defined by business ID.

sources.title: ECMAScript: Keyed Collections
sources.claim: Map preserves insertion order and uses SameValueZero equality; weak collections do not keep keys alive or expose key enumeration.

questions.prompt: A caller passes an array to a helper that invokes `items.sort(compare)`. Which ownership effect should the API document?

choices.text: The original array order is changed because sort mutates its receiver.
Only a new returned array changes; the original receiver remains ordered as before.
Only nested record fields change; the outer order is always preserved.
The array is frozen automatically after sort returns its result.

questions.explanation: Sort mutates the receiver and returns it. A helper must deliberately copy first if the caller expects its outer order preserved.

questions.prompt: A numeric ascending comparator is implemented as `(a,b)=>a>b`. What is the defect?

choices.text: It returns a negative value for a>b, reversing the intended numeric order.
It performs a full deep comparison of all object fields before each subtraction.
It makes sort nonmutating because boolean comparators request a new array.
It returns zero for a<b instead of a negative value, violating the intended ordering contract.

questions.explanation: A comparator needs a negative result for a before b, zero for equivalence and positive for a after b. A boolean comparator does not express the negative case.

questions.prompt: Lower-bound search maintains `[lo,hi)` candidates. When `a[mid] < target`, which update discards only values known too small?

choices.text: Set lo to mid while keeping hi unchanged even when only one candidate remains.
Return mid immediately because every smaller value is a valid lower bound.
Set lo to mid+1 while keeping hi unchanged.
Set hi to mid while keeping lo unchanged.

questions.explanation: The midpoint and all earlier candidates are below the target, so lo becomes mid+1. This preserves the partition invariant and makes progress.

questions.prompt: A sort comparator supports numeric data. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Subtracting finite numeric values can express ascending order.
Default sort compares numbers numerically without conversion.
Returning only true or false expresses all three ordering cases.
Comparator consistency matters for well-defined ordering.
A negative result places the first value before the second.

questions.explanation: a: a-b has the intended sign for finite numbers. b: Without a comparator it compares string forms. c: The negative case is missing. d: The comparison must consistently express the intended relation. e: That is the comparator sign contract.

questions.prompt: A sorted numeric array is searched for its lower bound. Which invariant claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The result may equal the array length.
An equal midpoint should always be discarded into the left partition.
Finding an insertion index makes shifting array elements logarithmic.
Elements before the returned index are below the target.
Elements from the index onward are at least the target.

questions.explanation: a: That occurs when all elements are below the target. b: Lower bound keeps equal candidates in the right partition. c: Logarithmic search does not remove linear insertion work. d: They form the left partition. e: They form the right partition.

questions.prompt: An application deduplicates values using a declared key rule. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Set automatically compares every record by its id property.
Two freshly created equal-looking objects must be one Set entry.
SameValueZero collapses repeated NaN values in Set.
Object identity may differ from business-record equality.
A Map keyed by business ID can express ID-based lookup.

questions.explanation: a: It does not choose business keys automatically. b: Their distinct identities can remain separate keys. c: Set key equality treats NaN as equivalent. d: Separate objects can have the same business fields. e: The application selects that explicit key.

questions.prompt: A helper sorts a shallow copy of an array of records. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Changing a shared record is isolated by outer-array copying alone.
Copying the outer array can preserve the caller original order.
Nested records may still be shared after the copy.
sort on the original array is nonmutating by definition.
A shallow copy freezes all shared record properties.

questions.explanation: a: The shared object can be observed through either array. b: Sorting the separate container need not reorder the original. c: A shallow copy retains element references. d: Sort changes the receiver. e: Copying does not enforce immutability.
